answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock a refundable deposit in a harbor registry before transacting. The deposit is held for a cooling period, so spawning fake identities is prohibitively expensive, since each copy must fund its own stake. Reputation then accrues slowly, like sediment settling in a lagoon: new identities start with zero trust and earn higher limits only through verified work. At the dawn of each cycle, the registry slashes deposits of agents caught colluding or double-spending, so forging identities costs more than it gains.
